checkpoints.note: The MLE receive path has already accepted the packet as an allowed MLE command, read command byte `0x0a` (`kCommandParentResponse`), and dispatched into the vulnerable Parent Response parser.

First project-side materialization of the malformed Response TLV on the crashing path. This statement copies the attacker-controlled Response TLV into fixed stack local `response` that is later over-read by `memcmp()`.

Because step 1 preserved header length 255 in `response`, this expression yields 255 even though the copied `ResponseTlv` only holds the 2-byte TLV header plus the fixed 8-byte response field. Reusing the raw TLV length here is the missing size obligation that makes the later `memcmp()` unsafe.
